about: This is the landing page from Mindloop Landing, published with the brief that produced it rather than as a screenshot. The palette runs deep blue #010713 underneath, and the type is Inter. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 455x800 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Take it on when the landing page needs a decided order before any new sections are added.

layout.title: Links collapse at one width
layout.body: The wordmark holds the left edge and the links run to the right of it, all of it set in Inter so the bar belongs to the page below rather than to a separate system. The bar sits over the 455x800 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it. If your own page has more sections, group them rather than widening the bar.

layout.title: Values you can check
layout.body: The list stays short (100px spacing steps), which is why the whole system can be checked by hand. Because the values are fixed, a substitution changes the look without changing the rhythm.

layout.title: The footer is a full composition
layout.body: Links are grouped into columns with the wordmark in its own block, which keeps a long footer readable instead of turning it into a list. The wordmark gets its own block, which keeps a long link list readable. Keep the accent for a single action.

layout.title: Top row, one action
layout.body: The row is sized from its own type rather than from a fixed header height. Copy this pattern when you need navigation that survives a loud first screen.

motion.title: Pointer states, nothing more
motion.body: Interaction is local to each control here (hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card and a sticky element that holds position while the content moves under it), so nothing on the page moves as a side effect. Press states are specified as well as hover, so a tap gives the same confirmation as a click.

motion.title: Almost no motion
motion.body: This one is delivered as a still composition at 455x800, so the hierarchy has to work without motion, and it does. Only the elements that respond to the pointer move.

editorial.title: What to change first in Mindloop Landing
editorial.body: When you drop your own media in, keep the crop and the layer order. The media is a still at 455x800. That placement is what keeps the copy legible. The composition is the reusable part, and it survives a different brand.

editorial.title: How Mindloop Landing sequences the first read
editorial.body: If your page currently leads with features, this is the order to copy: navigation, the headline, the stats row, the card grid and the background clip in front, the supporting detail after, and 100px spacing steps setting the distance. A SaaS reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: Why this composition works for SaaS
editorial.body: A tint layer over the media would have been the easy fix. The brief leaves it off. The copy still holds because 100px spacing steps keep the frame calm. Mindloop Landing states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

faq.question: Do I need React and Tailwind CSS to rebuild Mindloop Landing?
faq.answer: Mindloop Landing was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.
